output.summary: Wetland grass with a worldwide distribution, often forming extensive reed beds in damp ground or standing water. It bears dense dark-purple flower clusters that later look grey and silky; young shoots, sap, underground stems, seeds and other parts have documented food uses, though some are tough or scarce.
output.edibilityNote: Young shoots may be eaten raw or cooked; sap, underground stems, roots and seeds are also prepared as food, with some parts tough or scarce.
